jobs.title: Senior Analytics Engineer
jobs.description:
About BookNook:

BookNook is a research-driven high-impact tutoring solution that supports K–8 students in reading and math through live, synchronous tutoring sessions. Partnering with school districts and nonprofit organizations nationwide, BookNook delivers standards-aligned 1:1 or small-group instruction and structured tutoring models designed to strengthen foundational skills and accelerate student learning.

Since 2016, BookNook has supported more than 2.7K schools and partners across 40 states. Independent research demonstrates a clear link between high-impact tutoring and improved student outcomes. BookNook is committed to expanding access to strong academic support by connecting schools with skilled, supported tutors and scalable delivery models. Learn more at

Employment Type: Full-Time, W-2 permanent position

Data at BookNook:

Data at BookNook powers how we measure and communicate the impact of tutoring, and how districts, states, and research partners come to understand it. From state reporting feeds to the outcomes districts share with their school boards, we turn session and assessment data into insights for our customers, partners, and teams. We favor simple solutions to complex problems, build for scale over one-off answers, and treat student data with the care and responsibility it deserves.

This role will own that work end to end, evolving our data platform and driving data-informed decisions across BookNook to keep us at the forefront of high-impact tutoring.

The Role:

As BookNook’s Senior Analytics Engineer, you’ll own our data platform and the reporting built on it, delivering the state, district, and partner reporting our customers depend on. This is a hands-on technical role. You’ll administer our Snowflake environment, write and maintain the Python automations that power our reporting, and decide how our data is structured and managed. Your first year centers on the platform, state data feeds, and recurring client reporting. From there, you’ll lay the groundwork for longitudinal, year-over-year research on student outcomes and scalable operational reporting for executive leadership. You’ll be accountable not just for building our reporting, but for making sure people across BookNook actually use it and that it keeps getting better.

This is a senior Individual Contributor (IC) role, and you’ll be the dedicated owner of BookNook’s data function. You’ll report to the VP of Product Strategy and partner closely with engineering, security and IT, implementations, tutor operations, and executive leadership. As our data needs grow, you’ll help shape what the data function becomes.

About You:

You’re an experienced analytics or data engineer who is comfortable being the person who owns the data. You’re comfortable making decisions about how data is modeled, stored, and moved, pushing back thoughtfully on requests that won’t scale, and setting your own priorities. When someone asks for a number, you want to know what they’re trying to learn or decide, and you dig into what we actually have to find the closest honest answer, even when it isn’t the exact thing they asked for.

You can explain what the data shows, and what it doesn’t, to people who aren’t technical. You’re just as comfortable walking a district data team through a report as you are writing a pipeline, and you’d rather automate a process once than run it by hand every week. You build repeatable patterns rather than one-off analyses, so the answer to a question gets easier the second time someone asks it. You understand student data privacy standards, and you hold yourself to a standard that goes beyond what the law requires. You care about impact on the business and on the students and educators who rely on BookNook every day.

What you will be doing:

  • Data Platform Ownership: Own BookNook’s Snowflake environment and account, including cost and capacity management, data modeling, and the pipelines that turn raw data into reporting. Our SRE manages the pipeline from our production database into Snowflake, and you’ll partner closely with them as we move toward more real-time reporting.
  • End-to-End Project Ownership: Own data projects from the first question through delivery and upkeep, whether that’s a new state data feed, an automation, or a research dataset. Lead scoping conversations with stakeholders and present results internally as BookNook’s subject-matter expert on our data.
  • Data Privacy and Security: Make sure our company data privacy and PII policies are applied correctly across Snowflake and our other reporting tools and processes, and help enforce them. Partner closely with our IT and security team and our SRE to shape those policies at a company level, not just how they apply to our data stack.
  • Internal Data Partnership: Be the bridge between what people across BookNook ask for and what our data can actually answer. Understand the question behind each request, and help people move past data points that won’t support what they’re trying to show. Explain your findings clearly, including their limits, to non-technical audiences. Help teams across BookNook use our reports and tools on their own, so fewer requests need you.
  • Pipelines and Automation: Maintain and extend the automation engines, scheduled tasks, and one-click exports that support our customer-facing teams, including the tools that deliver data to states and partners, like SFTP and Airbyte. Continually find new places to remove manual data work from people’s plates, using scripts to bridge the gap where full automation isn’t in place yet.
  • Technical Partnerships and Reporting: Build strong working relationships with district admin and IT teams and with state data teams, staying current on state guidance and the data sharing requirements our partners need to meet to receive funding. Own state data feeds and district and partner reporting from start to finish, including custom data pulls, saved views, BI report builds, and the documentation that goes with them.
  • Onboarding and Process Improvement: Partner with engineering and implementations to design and refine processes for customer onboarding and ongoing reporting, especially for large customers, including reporting that helps validate setup and data quality.
  • Research and Partnerships Data: Build and maintain the foundations for outcomes research, including our assessment results data and tutor efficacy reporting. Lead the work to support longitudinal, year-over-year studies with research partners.
  • Operational Analytics: Provide executive leadership with the operational data they need and help scale dashboarding across the business. Use what you learn to propose improvements to the BookNook platform and services.

What we are looking for:

  • Experience: 5+ years in analytics engineering, data engineering, or a similar role, including time as the primary owner of a data platform, ideally at a small or growing company.
  • Snowflake Proficiency: Strong SQL skills and hands-on experience administering and building in Snowflake, including access control, cost management, and performance.
  • Python and Automation: Experience writing and maintaining Python scripts that run on a schedule to pull, transform, and deliver data, like automated reports, exports, and data feeds to partners.
  • BI and Reporting: Advanced experience building reports and dashboards in a BI tool such as Tableau, Power BI, Astrato, or similar.
  • Business and Data Judgment: The curiosity to learn our business model, our market, and how we work with districts, states, and partners well enough to know what our data can and can’t tell us, and to find a defensible answer when the exact one doesn’t exist.
  • Data Privacy: A working understanding of FERPA and related student privacy obligations, and a clear point of view on protecting data about minors.
  • Ownership and Prioritization: Comfort making decisions about how our data is modeled, stored, secured, and moved, prioritizing your own work, and saying no when a request doesn’t fit.
  • Communication and Relationships: Ability to explain technical concepts, findings, and tradeoffs to non-technical audiences, and to build strong relationships with internal teams and external partners, including district IT staff and state data teams.

Nice to have:

  • Experience in educational technology, specifically in K-12 environments.
  • Familiarity with educational assessments (such as i-Ready, DIBELS, or STAR) and the messiness of district-provided data.
  • Experience with data sharing and integration tools, such as SFTP and connectors like Airbyte.
  • Experience with real-time or streaming data pipelines.
  • Experience supporting research studies or longitudinal analysis.

We know imposter syndrome can sometimes discourage candidates from applying for jobs. If this role would make you excited to come to work every day, we encourage you to apply even if you don't meet all the requirements.

Perks and Benefits

  • Competitive salary: For this role, the salary range is $130K to $160K. Exact compensation may vary based on skills and experience.
  • Work remotely: Live and work wherever you like in the continental US.
  • Health insurance: We offer medical, dental, and vision insurance for all our team members.
  • Time to recharge: We offer flexible PTO, 11 paid holidays, and one company-wide week off.
  • 401(k): With 3% company match.
  • Home office setup: Get a laptop + $130 monthly stipend for home expenses.
  • Employee Recognition: We have built a culture based upon recognizing our coworkers’ value based achievements.

jobs.title: Paid Search Specialist
jobs.description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

jobs.title: Senior Commercial Pricing Analyst, USCAN PDx Radiopharma
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

The Senior Commercial Pricing Analyst is an experienced individual contributor who supports the USCAN PDx Radiopharma commercial organization through independent pricing analytics, deal evaluation, reporting, and ownership of core pricing processes. The role leads analytical work for pricing decisions, Commercial Deal Review (CDR), discount and exception management, price realization, and ongoing pricing performance, and provides clear recommendations to the Pricing Manager and commercial leaders.

Working closely with the Pricing Manager and cross-functional partners, the senior analyst manages complex analyses with minimal supervision, turning customer, product, contract, and financial data into actionable insights that support disciplined pricing decisions and profitable growth. The role serves as a trusted subject-matter resource for pricing data, models, and governance requirements in a regulated healthcare environment, while providing the analytical expertise and independent ownership needed to support broader pricing leadership responsibilities.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities

Pricing Analytics & Reporting

  • Independently perform recurring and ad hoc pricing analyses across products, customers, channels, and commercial segments, and present findings and recommendations.
  • Own the monitoring of key pricing KPIs, including price realization, discount levels, gross-to-net performance, and margin trends, and proactively escalate material changes with proposed actions.
  • Lead customer, product, and contract-level variance analyses to identify pricing trends, leakage, and opportunities.
  • Build and maintain scenario models and sensitivity analyses to evaluate alternative pricing and deal structures.
  • Analyze historical pricing and customer purchasing patterns to develop pricing recommendations.
  • Design, develop, and maintain pricing reports, dashboards, and performance scorecards for the commercial team and leadership.
  • Partner with Analytics and Finance to improve pricing visibility, define reporting requirements, and validate outputs in tools such as Power BI.

Commercial Deal & CDR Support

  • Lead preparation of analyses for Commercial Deal Review (CDR), Deal Desk, and other pricing governance forums, and provide a clear recommendation to the Pricing Manager.
  • Evaluate proposed customer pricing, discounts, rebates, and contract structures, including complex or non-standard arrangements.
  • Prepare financial analyses showing margin impact, price realization, and key economic trade-offs for proposed commercial arrangements, and explain the assumptions and risks to stakeholders.
  • Develop and maintain standardized deal models and analytical templates to improve the consistency and speed of deal evaluation.
  • Track approved deals, pricing commitments, and exceptions to support post-approval monitoring.
  • Conduct post-deal analyses comparing approved assumptions with actual pricing and commercial performance, and share lessons learned to refine future deal guidance.

Price & Discount Management

  • Manage day-to-day maintenance of commercial price lists, pricing files, effective dates, and supporting documentation.
  • Monitor discounting activity and pricing exceptions against established policies and approval thresholds, and follow up with commercial teams on non-compliant activity.
  • Maintain pricing exception records, approvals, and supporting documentation, and ensure audit readiness.
  • Analyze discount and exception trends to identify pricing leakage or recurring commercial patterns, and recommend policy or process changes.
  • Lead periodic pricing changes and implementation activities across commercial systems and processes.

Pricing Strategy Support

  • Lead the analytical work for annual and lifecycle pricing initiatives, including list-price changes and customer pricing actions.
  • Conduct customer and market segmentation analyses to identify pricing opportunities and recommend actions.
  • Develop analyses supporting pricing optimization and value-based pricing initiatives.
  • Evaluate and communicate the financial impact of proposed pricing strategies across customers, products, and segments.
  • Conduct competitive and market analyses and translate the findings into pricing recommendations.

Government Pricing & Compliance Support

  • Perform analyses assessing how discounts, rebates, and commercial contract structures may affect government pricing metrics.
  • Lead data validation, documentation, reconciliations, and analytical support associated with AMP, Best Price, 340B, and other applicable government pricing requirements.
  • Maintain organized documentation and analytical audit trails supporting pricing decisions.
  • Partner with the Pricing Manager, Market Access, Finance, and Compliance to identify and flag downstream government pricing implications of commercial decisions before they are finalized.

Process Improvement & Pricing Enablement

  • Identify and lead opportunities to automate and streamline recurring pricing analyses and reporting.
  • Develop and maintain pricing tools, models, templates, and standard operating processes.
  • Own pricing data quality, working with Analytics, Finance, and IT to resolve data issues affecting pricing reports.
  • Create documentation and training materials for pricing policies, processes, and tools, and train commercial partners on their use.
  • Mentor and provide guidance to junior analysts or team members on analytical methods, tools, and pricing processes.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Business, Economics, Analytics, Healthcare, or related field. MBA or advanced degree is a plus.
  • 4–7 years of experience in pricing, commercial analytics, finance, contracting, revenue management, sales operations, or related analytical function.
  • Strong analytical and quantitative skills with a proven ability to translate complex data into actionable business insights and recommendations.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including financial modeling, large-data analysis, and scenario modeling.
  • Experience independently developing reports, dashboards, or data visualizations.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present to commercial and finance leaders.
  • High attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines with minimal supervision.

Preferred

  • Experience within pharmaceuticals, radiopharmaceuticals, healthcare, medical devices, nuclear medicine, or another regulated industry.
  • Experience supporting commercial pricing, contracting, Deal Desk, or sales operations, including evaluating complex deals.
  • Hands-on experience with Power BI, Salesforce, SAP, Model N, Revitas, or similar commercial/pricing platforms.
  • Working knowledge of U.S. pharmaceutical government pricing concepts, including AMP, Best Price, Medicaid, 340B, Medicare, and VA/FSS.
  • Experience working with large transactional or customer-level datasets.
  • Experience mentoring or informally leading other analysts.

Competencies

  • Strong analytical thinking and problem solving
  • Commercial and financial acumen
  • Independent judgment and ownership of outcomes
  • Intellectual curiosity and willingness to challenge assumptions
  • High attention to detail and data accuracy
  • Ability to translate complex analyses into clear business recommendations
  • Influence and stakeholder management across Commercial, Finance, and Compliance
  • Strong organization, prioritization, and execution
  • Ability to coach and mentor others
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, regulated environment
  • Continuous-improvement mindset
  • Sound judgment when handling sensitive commercial and pricing information

jobs.description:
About Positron AI

Positron AI is building next-generation AI inference accelerators designed from the ground up for low-latency, high-throughput large language model inference. Chips built for the training era keep running into two walls at inference time: memory bandwidth and chip-to-chip networking. We designed our architecture to break through both. Our first-generation Atlas systems are already in production on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Asimov, our first custom ASIC, takes that architecture to silicon. In simulations, Asimov delivers several times more tokens per dollar and tokens per watt than leading GPUs, at a fraction of the power. Paired in our Titan system, Asimov is built to serve models beyond 16 trillion parameters. In September 2026, we raised $875 million at a $5 billion valuation. NEA led the round, joined by Atreides Management, Valor Equity Partners, and others, to bring Asimov and Titan to market. Our team includes engineers from Groq, Lambda, NVIDIA, Meta, F5, and many other industry leaders.

Role Overview

As a Developer Platform Engineer, you will build the layer that lets AI coding agents do real work on our simulators. We have a full simulation ecosystem built on one shared hardware model, and demand on it is growing in every direction at once: more chip programs, new model architectures, larger deployment topologies, and customers who want modeling tooling. We cannot scale by adding people alone. You will work with every engineer on the team to make routine simulator work, such as adding commands, running experiments, and bringing up new models, something an agent can do end to end, with evidence.

The work is platform engineering with a verification mindset: the interfaces agents call, the workflows they follow, and the guardrails that keep agent-written changes trustworthy. Our test lead continues to own testing practice; you will build the agent layer on top of it.

Key Responsibilities

Agent Interfaces

  • Design and build the MCP servers and APIs that let AI coding agents drive our simulators end to end, so that running a simulation, reading a trace, and comparing against a reference all happen from one call.
  • Make the simulators legible to agents and people alike through clear CLI and API design, structured outputs, reproducible runs, and useful error messages.

Agent Workflows

  • Build agent workflows for simulator development in which an agent implements or extends a hardware command's functional, dependency, cost, and cycle models and lands it with test evidence.
  • Partner with the model architecture engineer to automate new-model bring-up from model specification to simulator coverage.

Guardrails and Measurement

  • Build CI guardrails for agent-produced changes, including golden-reference generation, static analysis, known-good comparisons, and provenance on every result.
  • Measure what agents get right and wrong, and feed those findings back into the tooling.

Required Qualifications

  • 4+ years of experience in developer tooling, developer platforms, or infrastructure engineering.
  • Demonstrated experience building tooling that LLM coding agents use in production, such as MCP servers or tool APIs, agent workflows in CI, evaluation harnesses, or agent-driven code generation with verification.
  • A strong understanding of CI/CD and test infrastructure, including flaky-test detection, golden-reference testing, and static analysis in CI.
  • Hands-on experience designing CLIs and APIs that are easy to use correctly and hard to use wrongly, with structured logging and reproducible builds.
  • Ability to design systems in which agent-produced changes carry evidence and cannot land unverified.
  • Strong Rust skills, or expert-level C/C++ skills and a willingness to work in Rust day to day, along with proficiency in Python for tooling.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain to engineers what the agent layer can and cannot be trusted with, and why.

Preferred Qualifications

  • A background in simulation, compilers, or hardware.
  • Experience running evaluations of agent or model performance on engineering tasks.

Leveling & Scope

While this role is currently posted at a specific level, we are a growth-oriented organization and are open to hiring at a more senior level for the right candidate. Please note that this job description serves as a focused but generalized overview of the role; specific responsibilities and impact expectations will be tailored to the experience and seniority of the final hire.

Why Join Us?

  • You will define how AI coding agents do trustworthy engineering work on a real chip simulation stack, a problem few teams anywhere are tackling in production.
  • Your tooling will multiply the output of every engineer on the team as we scale across chip programs, model architectures, and customers.

Compensation & Benefits

The base salary range for this role is Mid: $160,000-$220,000, Senior: $220,000–$270,000, Principal: $270,000-$350,000.

Please note that the figures provided represent the base salary range only and do not include other elements of our total compensation package, equity, or comprehensive benefits.

At Positron AI, we value the unique expertise each candidate brings. While the range above reflects our typical expectation for the position, we reserve the flexibility to exceed this range for candidates whose specialized skills, significant experience, or unique qualifications fall outside the standard scope of the role. Final offers are determined based on a variety of factors, including internal equity, and individual impact.

Benefits & Perks

We want you to do your best work and feel confident that you and your family are taken care of. That means comprehensive coverage, real time to rest, and support for your future.

About the Company:

The mining industry has steadily become worse at finding new ore deposits, requiring >10X more capital to make discoveries compared to 30 years ago. The easy-to-find, near-surface deposits have largely been found, and the industry has chronically under-invested in new exploration technology, relying on the manual techniques of yesteryear – even as demand accelerates for copper, lithium, and other metals to build electric vehicles, renewable energy, and data centers.

KoBold builds AI models for mineral exploration and deploys those models—alongside our novel sensors—to guide decisions on KoBold-owned-and-operated exploration programs. Since our founding in 2018, KoBold has become by far both the largest independent mineral exploration company and the largest exploration technology developer. Our data scientists and software engineers, who come from leading technology companies, jointly lead exploration programs with our renowned exploration geologists.

KoBold has proven its first discovery with materially less capital than the industry average and found one of the best copper deposits ever discovered: the copper is far more concentrated than the global average of copper mines, and this asset alone is expected to generate meaningful revenue for decades. KoBold has a portfolio of more than 80 other projects, each of which has the potential for another high-quality discovery.

KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.

About the position

In this role, you will lead evaluations of potential properties for acquisition, generate targets, and design and oversee field programs from target definition through to resource expansion. You will be part of a multidisciplinary team and will work closely with data scientists, using KoBold’s technology to help guide our field programs and decision-making. You will also work directly with our senior technical advisors and with the executive team on making the investment case for acquisitions and field programs.

Ultimately, your role is to help KoBold make valuable discoveries by identifying opportunities with rigorous evaluation and by ensuring that we safely and effectively conduct our field programs.

Responsibilities
  • Demonstrate in all activities a commitment to the highest standards in health and safety, environment, and community relations
  • Rigorously analyze geoscientific datasets across a range of scales from provinces to prospects to determine exploration potential and to identify, rank, and prioritize exploration targets
  • Design, budget, permit, and execute field programs ranging from geological mapping and sampling of grass roots prospects through to large drilling programs on advanced projects, with leading industry practice in data acquisition and validation
  • Provide technical guidance and support to local in-country project teams during the design and execution of exploration programs, including site visits and engagement with other project stakeholders (e.g., community representatives, regulatory authorities, and joint venture partners)
  • Work collaboratively with data scientist colleagues to conceive and implement insightful analytical methods
Qualifications

A great Exploration Geologist candidate will have:

  • Strong technical knowledge of one or more ore deposit types. Experience working on sediment-hosted stratiform copper or magmatic sulfide deposits will be considered an advantage
  • Excellence in generative analysis ranging from new concepts to integration, interpretation, and modeling of large datasets
  • Good field skills and experience conducting field programs across a range of project stages from grassroots prospects through to advanced projects with significant drilling campaigns
  • Baseline level of proficiency in standard desktop software packages (e.g., ArcGIS or QGIS)
  • Strong leadership skills including the ability to motivate and inspire others, to share ownership and responsibility for project outcomes, and to work effectively in collaborative, interdisciplinary teams

  • Demonstrated commitment to high standards of health and safety in the workplace

  • Knowledge of geostatistics and/or other statistical methods relevant for analysis of geoscientific data
  • International experience, particularly in the Central African Copperbelt

Note: Candidates who are specialists in geochemistry or geophysics but open to doing significant project work are encouraged to apply.

What to Expect

Joining KoBold means getting the opportunity for hands-on exposure to our exploration projects around the world. All employees are expected to travel to project sites, with a minimum of one week per year. Field-facing and technical roles spend significantly more time in the field.

jobs.title: Penetration Tester - Infrastructure & Red Team (Canada)
jobs.description:
Packetlabs was built by an ethical hacker after seeing vulnerability assessments presented as penetration tests. Our slogan "Identify Risks Before They Become Headlines" drives at the importance of not providing our clients with a false sense of security.

We are a passionate team of highly trained, proactive ethical hackers. We provide expert-level penetration testing services that are thorough and tailored to help foster a safe digital space where everyone has the right to privacy and security. Packetlabs consultants find weaknesses others overlook and continuously learn new ways to evade controls. We hold ourselves to a very high standard.

To do so, weonlyhire individuals with the same drive and passion.

The Ethical Hacker – Infrastructure & Red Team is responsible for planning, executing, and reporting on infrastructure penetration testing, cloud security assessments, Active Directory security assessments, and adversary simulation engagements. The role evaluates the effectiveness of client security controls by identifying, validating, and demonstrating exploitable security vulnerabilities across enterprise infrastructure using industry-recognized offensive security methodologies.

Working independently and collaboratively with other security consultants, the Ethical Hacker performs offensive security assessments across on-premises, hybrid, and cloud environments while contributing to red team operations, purple team exercises, and advanced security testing engagements. The role provides technical guidance to clients through detailed reporting and presentations while contributing to the continuous improvement of Packetlabs' offensive security methodologies, tooling, and service offerings.

Who we are looking for

  • Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related discipline; equivalent practical experience will be considered.
  • Minimum of 3 years of professional experience performing infrastructure penetration testing, red teaming, adversary simulation, or offensive security consulting.
  • Demonstrated experience conducting penetration testing across enterprise infrastructure, including Windows, Linux, Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, cloud platforms, and enterprise networking.
  • Experience performing internal and external network penetration testing, privilege escalation, Active Directory security assessments, and lateral movement testing.
  • Experience assessing cloud environments, including AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform.
  • Strong understanding of enterprise networking, authentication technologies, identity management, cloud security, and offensive security methodologies.
  • Experience using industry-standard offensive security frameworks, tools, and tradecraft.
  • Excellent technical writing, presentation, and communication skills, with the ability to communicate findings to both technical and executive stakeholders.
  • Industry certifications such as OSCP, OSEP, CRTO, CRTE, CARTP, CARTA, CREST CRT, CREST CCT, PNPT, GPEN, GXPN, or equivalent are considered an asset. OSCP or equivalent demonstrated technical capability is strongly preferred.
  • Experience participating in Red Team, Purple Team, adversary simulation, or threat emulation engagements is considered an asset.
  • Customer-first mentality. You are a great communicator with clients, project managers, and teammates. Rapid responses and on time.
  • You deliver work that you take pride in. Your work is an autograph of your excellence.
  • You dig deeper into every finding. Doesn't stop until impact is proven.
  • You are comfortable being uncomfortable. Goes towards obstacles, not away from them. Consulting isn't your typical job and requires adapting to rapidly changing environments.
  • You are always learning. Cybersecurity is changing every day, and you need to keep up or want to keep up. Be deeply aware of your skillset and be willing to improve.
  • You are self-motivated and dependable.
  • You are humble. Egos don't have a place at Packetlabs.

What you’ll be doing

  • Infrastructure Security Assessments
    • Plan and execute infrastructure penetration testing engagements across on-premises, hybrid, cloud, wireless, and enterprise network environments.
    • Perform internal and external network penetration testing to identify, validate, and exploit security vulnerabilities using manual testing methodologies and industry-standard offensive security tools.
    • Assess enterprise technologies including Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), Windows and Linux environments, virtualization platforms, cloud services, and supporting infrastructure.
    • Evaluate cloud environments including AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform to identify configuration weaknesses, privilege escalation opportunities, identity risks, and cloud security vulnerabilities.
    • Assess containerized environments, Kubernetes platforms, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud-native technologies where applicable.
  • Red Team & Adversary Simulation
    • Participate in and lead adversary simulation, red team, and objective-based security engagements in accordance with established methodologies and client objectives.
    • Execute offensive security operations across the attack lifecycle, including reconnaissance, initial access, persistence, privilege escalation, credential access, lateral movement, defense evasion, command and control, and objective execution.
    • Support purple team engagements by working collaboratively with defensive teams to validate detections, improve monitoring capabilities, and strengthen defensive controls.
    • Develop and execute attack scenarios that demonstrate realistic business impact while maintaining client system integrity.
  • Client Delivery & Reporting
    • Prepare comprehensive technical reports that clearly communicate vulnerabilities, attack paths, business impact, risk ratings, and remediation recommendations.
    • Present assessment findings to technical teams, executive stakeholders, and client leadership.
    • Provide technical guidance on remediation strategies, security architecture, and defensive improvements.
    • Manage assigned engagements while ensuring delivery quality, timelines, and client expectations are achieved.
  • Technical Leadership & Continuous Improvement
    • Maintain expertise in offensive security methodologies, infrastructure security, cloud technologies, Active Directory security, and emerging attack techniques.
    • Contribute to the development and continuous improvement of testing methodologies, internal tooling, technical documentation, and service offerings.
    • Participate in technical research, automation initiatives, internal training, and knowledge-sharing activities.
    • Collaborate with consulting teams to strengthen technical quality, consistency, and service delivery across the Offensive Security practice.
    • Perform other duties as assigned.

How is success defined

  • Performance in this role is evaluated using a combination of technical, operational, and client-focused measures, including but not limited to:
    • Successful delivery of infrastructure penetration testing and adversary simulation engagements within established quality, budget, and timeline expectations.
    • Accuracy, completeness, and technical quality of client reports and deliverables.
    • Demonstrated expertise across enterprise infrastructure, cloud security, Active Directory, and offensive security methodologies.
    • Positive client feedback regarding technical expertise, communication, and professionalism.
    • Contribution to technical research, methodology development, automation, and knowledge-sharing initiatives.
    • Effective collaboration with Delivery Managers, Project Managers, and consulting team members.
    • Ongoing professional development through certifications, research, and technical skill advancement.

Why us?

  • The opportunity to work on high-stakes hardware engagements where your judgment and bench skills genuinely matter
  • Receive immediate and ongoing offensive security training, mentorship, and professional development to advance your technical capabilities
  • Play a key role in shaping the growth, direction, and methodology of Packetlabs' expanding hardware practice
  • A leadership team that values substance, quality, and disciplined execution
  • Collaboration with a highly skilled team of security professionals who are passionate about technical excellence and raising the bar
  • Competitive compensation and growth opportunity
  • GRRSP with corporate matching in Canada
  • Participation in corporate benefit plans within Canada
  • Flexible work environment that empowers employees to do their best work
  • Fully remote within Canada

At Smart Working, we believe your job should not only look right on paper but also feel right every day. This isn’t just another remote opportunity - it’s about finding where you truly belong, no matter where you are. From day one, you’re welcomed into a genuine community that values your growth and well-being.

Our mission is simple: to break down geographic barriers and connect skilled professionals with outstanding global teams and products for full-time, long-term roles. We help you discover meaningful work with teams that invest in your success, where you’re empowered to grow personally and professionally.

Join one of the highest-rated workplaces on Glassdoor and experience what it means to thrive in a truly remote-first world.

As a Cloud Engineer (Backend / DevOps-leaning), you will take responsibility for designing, building and maintaining AWS infrastructure using Terraform and Infrastructure as Code. This is an ongoing, long-term opportunity focused on reliable cloud infrastructure and its supporting delivery processes.

You will manage EC2 and other core infrastructure components, support CI/CD pipelines for infrastructure changes, and implement and maintain security and compliance controls.

Responsibilities

  • Develop, maintain and improve AWS cloud infrastructure using Terraform and Infrastructure as Code (IaC).

jobs.title: Physician (MD/DO) - Medical AI Evaluation
jobs.description:
About the company

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. This is a task-based, independent contractor opportunity, not an employment relationship. Participation is limited to this project.

Project Highlights

  • Earnings per approved task: a fixed rate for each task, set in advance
  • Fully self-scheduled: no minimum hours and no set schedule; you choose which tasks to take and when
  • Remote: open to US-licensed physicians based in eligible US states
  • No patient contact, no malpractice exposure: you review written clinical cases
  • All contributors are license-verified physicians
  • $50 one-time onboarding reward, paid once your first task on the project is approved

What this project involves

We're looking for physicians (MD/DO) with an active, unrestricted US medical license to evaluate clinical EHR vignettes for a medical AI evaluation project. General and internal medicine are the main focus. Each task is a written clinical case, assessed against the project's acceptance criteria. Contributors may:

  • Evaluate clinical EHR vignettes paired with a question, a proposed answer, and a distractor "trap" answer across diagnosis and treatment tasks, spanning cardiovascular, nervous, hematologic, respiratory, digestive, urinary, reproductive, musculoskeletal, and integumentary systems;
  • Score the clinical reasoning quality of benchmark items: vignette accuracy and completeness, whether the vignette gives the answer away, answer correctness and gradeability, and trap quality;
  • Check whether the reasoning chain reaches the answer from vignette facts alone, correct reasoning traces, and write short rationales.

Each case receives three independent blind reads, followed by physician adjudication. Real clinical complexity only. You're improving the AI tools you'll eventually use yourself.

What we look for

This project is a good fit for US-licensed physicians looking for a flexible, time-limited project they can fit around their other commitments. Ideally, contributors will have:

  • Medical degree (MD or DO) and an active, unrestricted US medical license (verified at onboarding and re-checked monthly);
  • Board certification or completed residency training, with direct patient care experience (attending-level preferred). Practising or retired physicians welcome;
  • Broad, multi-system diagnostic and treatment experience (internal, family, emergency, or hospital medicine);
  • Strong clinical reasoning: differential diagnosis, next-step management, and application of evidence-based guidelines;
  • Prior experience in medical AI evaluation, clinical content or exam-question review, or medical annotation/QA (a plus);
  • Strong written English (C1+).

This project is not suitable for medical students, unlicensed medical graduates, non-physician clinicians (NPs, PAs, nurses, pharmacists), or non-clinical healthcare titles.

How it works

Apply → Pass qualification(s) → Join the project → Complete tasks → Get paid for approved tasks

Flexibility

You decide whether, when, and how much to contribute. There are no minimum hours, set schedules, or required availability. Task availability varies with project phases. Tasks are submitted through the platform and are approved when they meet the project’s acceptance criteria.

Earnings

Earnings are paid only for completed and approved tasks. Each task type has a fixed rate. There is no time tracking and no hour logging. There are no tiers or speed adjustments to the rate. QA and adjudication tasks have a higher per-task rate.

  • $50 one-time onboarding reward, paid once your first task on the project is approved.
  • Quality incentives: additional earnings for high-quality approved tasks, on terms set out in the project guidelines.

jobs.title: Google Ads Media Buyer / Growth Strategist
jobs.description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

jobs.title: Senior Engineer - ESD
jobs.description:
About Megaport

We’re not your typical tech company – and we don’t want to be. Megaport is the global leader in Network as a Service (NaaS), and has transformed the way businesses connect to the cloud, data centers, and each other. We’re publicly listed on the Australian Stock Exchange and partnered with the biggest names in tech like Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Oracle, IBM, and more. Headquartered in Brisbane with a crew of over 600 people spread across Asia-Pacific, Europe, and the Americas, our employees enjoy an environment that is collaborative, supportive, and (actually) fun.

Our Team Culture

We’re a team of problem solvers, pixel pushers, code slingers, and cloud fanatics. Culture is more than a poster on the wall here – collaboration beats hierarchy, curiosity fuels our growth, and everyone’s voice matters. We take our work seriously, but not ourselves. We work across time zones to execute on our global vision, trust each other to get things done, and never compromise our values for commercial gain. Most importantly, we place our customers at the center of everything we do.
We’re committed to increasing representation in the tech industry and welcome applicants from all backgrounds. Don’t meet every requirement? That’s okay. If you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply.

The Role

We are seeking a highly experienced engineer to join our Edge Services team, responsible for building and evolving Megaport’s edge compute platform. This platform underpins our Virtual Network Function (VNF) products and the networking systems that power them globally.

In this role, you will operate at the intersection of distributed systems, networking, and cloud-native infrastructure. You will be a key technical leader shaping the compute and networking stack, driving architectural decisions, and ensuring scalability, reliability, and performance across our edge platform. Beyond deep technical contribution, you will act as a central advisor within your domain - guiding strategy, mentoring engineers, and influencing outcomes across teams.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Influence the evolution of Megaport’s edge compute and networking platform

  • Architect and optimize bare metal infrastructure for high-performance VNF workloads

  • Design and implement networking solutions leveraging EVPN and host-based technologies

  • Act as a key technical advisor for a defined domain or program of work

  • Drive technical strategy, standards, and system-wide design patterns across teams

  • Troubleshoot and resolve complex, high-impact issues across distributed systems

  • Collaborate cross-functionally to align engineering efforts with business and product goals

  • Provide clear and proactive communication to stakeholders, including leadership and non-technical audiences

  • Break down initiatives into deliverables, estimate work, and validate team estimates

  • Identify and manage technical debt while driving continuous platform improvements

  • Mentor engineers on system design, trade-offs, and architectural thinking

  • Champion innovation and promote best practices across the engineering organization

  • Identify opportunities to standardize systems and improve platform consistency

What We Are Looking For

  • Experience as a senior or principal-level engineer working on distributed systems, cloud platforms, or networking infrastructure

  • Deep understanding of networking technologies including MPLS, VXLAN and EVPN

  • Practical expertise with linux networking and DPDK

  • Experience designing and operating platforms supporting virtualised network functions (VNFs)

  • Proven ability to design scalable, resilient systems and evaluate architectural trade-offs

  • Experience leading technical strategy and influencing engineering direction across teams

  • You have excellent written and verbal communication skills

  • You can work collaboratively in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment

What We Offer

  • Flexible working environments

  • Birthday Leave

  • Generous study and training allowance + 5 days paid study leave

  • Creative, fun, and contemporary workspaces

  • Motivated team of industry experts and new talent

  • Celebrated success with ‘Legend’ and ‘Kudos’ Awards

  • Health and wellness program

  • Opportunities for career growth and potential for global intra-company transfers for interested candidates

If you have any questions, please reach out to Megaport's Talent Acquisition Team at
NOTE: All Megaport business correspondence is conducted via our business email accounts (@megaport.com). If you have any concerns, please reach out to Megaport's careers team directly and we will verify the legitimacy of any communication. Megaport will not ask you to create an account via Microsoft teams, and does not associate with any email accounts under "@megaportau.com".
All applications will be treated in confidence.
Please see Part 2 of our Privacy Policy to see what information Megaport collects from job applicants, why, and how we store and use it. Note that you’re entitled to know what personal data of yours Megaport holds, to request updates, rectification, and in some circumstances restriction or deletion thereof if you object (you being entitled to withdraw your consent to our holding your information at any time). Please see Part 5 of our Privacy Policy for more details on this and how to contact Megaport's data protection officer if you have any further privacy-related questions. Candidates who meet the selection criteria will be invited to attend an interview. Strictly no Recruitment Agencies.

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. We're looking for a Senior Customer Success Manager, Strategic Accounts to own and grow relationships with some of Bask Health's most important merchant customers.

This role is responsible for the long-term success of strategic accounts, from onboarding and adoption through retention, renewals, and expansion.

You'll serve as a primary post-sale relationship owner for a portfolio of high-value customers using Bask Health to operate and grow their telehealth businesses.

Our customers include entrepreneurs, e-commerce operators, healthcare businesses, and other organizations building direct-to-consumer telehealth experiences.

This role sets technical direction for FHIR-based digital quality measure (dQM) specification work, serves as the primary technical point of contact with CMS and other clients for topics related to digital quality measurement, including FHIR, and is responsible for mentoring a small team of measure developers and analysts. The ideal candidate has hands-on experience translating clinical quality measures into CQL and FHIR-based specifications and is comfortable operating across the full dQM lifecycle, from measure concept through annual maintenance updates.

This position sits within AIR's Quality Measurement & Improvement portfolio, which supports CMS accountability and quality reporting programs across clinician, hospital, and post-acute/nursing home settings. You will work closely with QM&I leadership to grow the organization's technical capability in FHIR-based digital quality measurement.

Engagements are typically project-based, part-time, and may vary in duration and hours depending on project needs.

Candidates hired for the position may work remotely within the United States (U.S.) or from one of our U.S. office locations. This does not include U.S. territories. 

About AIR:

Founded in 1946 and headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, the American Institutes for Research (AIR) is a nonpartisan, not-for-profit organization that conducts behavioral and social science research and delivers technical assistance to address some of the most pressing challenges in the United States and globally. We generate evidence and apply data-driven solutions that expand opportunities and improve lives for all.

  • Partner with AIR's broader capability to align FHIR/interoperability practices across projects.

  • Vet and evaluate technical partners and platforms for proposal efforts.

  • Serve as AIR’s FHIR standard expert on CMS eCQM contracts, representing AIR in client meetings, technical expert panels, and standards workgroups.
  • Build and maintain strategic partnerships with public agencies, nonprofits, philanthropic organizations, and academic institutions.
  • Contribute to AIR’s organizational learning by sharing insights, innovations, and lessons learned from TA practice.

Qualifications:

Education, Knowledge, and Experience

  • Master’s degree in health informatics, computer science, public health, nursing, or a related field with a minimum of 11 years of or relevant experience.
  • 7+ years of experience in health care quality measurement, with direct, hands-on experience authoring QDM-based eCQMs and FHIR-based dQMs required.
  • Working knowledge of FHIR resources and implementation guides relevant to quality measurement (US Core, QI-Core, Data Exchange for Quality Measures, or similar).

Executar pentests de aplicações web, APIs e mobile dentro de escopos definidos, com evidência reproduzível e impacto claro.

jobs.description:
Job Description:

Job Title - Senior Project Manager

Location - Remote, UK Based

Type - Permanent, Full-time 37.5 hours


About Velonetic

For more than 100 years, Velonetic has helped keep the London insurance market moving. Our specialist people, proven processes and technology make complex insurance operations simpler, faster and more reliable for more than 400 market participants, across the insurance lifecycle from placement and premium processing to claims and settlement.

Now we are evolving with the market, pairing deep insurance expertise with data, automation and modern technology to reduce friction, improve accuracy and deliver better outcomes for our customers. Our culture is built on collaboration, respect, ownership, boldness and integrity, and you will have the opportunity to do work that matters at the heart of a globally important insurance marketplace.


Role purpose

Join us as Senior Project Manager and lead the technology change that keeps the London market moving. You will take ownership of complex, business-critical projects and programmes across our portfolio, with real accountability for scope, schedule, cost, quality, risk, governance, stakeholder engagement and benefits, including work delivered with strategic partners and suppliers. We are looking for a technically credible delivery leader with London Insurance Market experience, who knows how to land change safely for the people who rely on it.

You will work alongside internal teams, market stakeholders, architects, operational teams, suppliers and delivery partners to build realistic, transparent plans, constructively challenge assumptions and keep end-to-end ownership. Your insight will give our leaders the evidence they need to make confident decisions on priorities, resources, risks and trade-offs.


What you will do

  • Lead technology projects and programmes end to end, from mobilisation through implementation, transition and closure.
  • Own integrated plans, milestones, dependencies, resources, risks, issues, assumptions and decisions.
  • Hold strategic technology partners and other third-party suppliers to account for the outcomes they deliver.
  • Connect business requirements, solution architecture, technical design, testing, deployment and operational readiness.
  • Represent Velonetic in market and delivery governance forums, building stakeholder trust and delivering with integrity.
  • Deliver within the standards, stage gates and controls set by the Head of Programme Delivery.

What you will own

  • Give leaders accurate, insight-led reporting on RAG status, milestones, risks, issues, dependencies, decisions and change requests, including Steering Committee and board updates that support timely decisions.
  • Manage budgets, forecasts, supplier costs and change control so that spend stays aligned with approved plans and business cases.
  • Lead implementation readiness, testing, cutover, warranty and handover into live service, using phased transition where it reduces operational or market risk.
  • Bring teams, SMEs, architects and suppliers together around clear priorities, keep documentation current, apply proportionate governance, and coach project managers to strengthen delivery practice.

What you will bring

  • Extensive experience delivering complex technology programmes, including software delivery, systems integration, data, workflow and platform change, with a proven record of controlled delivery across scope, schedule, cost, quality, risk and benefits.
  • Hands-on technical delivery credibility, with the confidence to engage architects and engineers on requirements, design, integration, testing, release and cutover, challenge estimates and sequencing, and translate technical issues into clear business impacts and choices.
  • Substantial experience delivering technology change within the London Insurance Market (for example Lloyd's, insurers, reinsurers, brokers or market services providers), and a clear understanding of market processes and the impact of change on market participants.
  • Experience managing delivery through outsourced technology partners, including joint planning, supplier challenge, performance management and commercial escalation.
  • The ability to keep delivery on track in uncertain environments by exposing assumptions and risks early.
  • A track record of influencing senior and Executive-level stakeholders, with clear, engaging communication and the judgement to balance pace, quality and operational resilience.

What will set you apart

  • Working knowledge of London Market governance, regulatory and market-body requirements, and the wider insurance, reinsurance and Lloyd's ecosystem.
  • Experience leading transformation or modernisation programmes alongside an outsourced delivery partner.
  • Knowledge of Agile, hybrid and traditional delivery methodologies, ideally supported by a certification such as PMP, PRINCE2 Practitioner, MSP or APM ChPP.

Investment In Training and Development

We offer a comprehensive range of training and career development opportunities, a structured induction programme, tailored job training as well as mentoring and support for relevant sponsored professional qualifications. We’re developing an environment where people can grow and harness their careers and skills to be the best that they can be to focus on the long term.

Our Culture

Here at Velonetic we support with care and compassion. We are constantly evolving our initiatives around equality, diversity, and inclusion to ensure that everyone feels equally involved and supported in the workplace no matter of who they are or what they do. We are proud of the culture we are creating to ensure that our commitment is ongoing and have a diverse mix of employees working within an inclusive environment and culture to create a high performing workforce led by talented leaders. We aspire to be recognised for our innovative and modern thinking approach.

Employee Benefits

As part of our competitive remuneration package, flexible benefits are available. There is an option to “flex up and down” on specific benefits, for example buy or sell annual leave, Private Medical Benefit, Dental and Travel Insurance.

You will also have access to ‘Perks at Work’, a discount store to purchase gift cards at reduced rates and get discounts on holidays, restaurants, activities, groceries and more.

DXC Recruitment Team will be engaging with all candidate applications on behalf of Velonetic. DXC will be managing the recruitment throughout the onboarding process.

At DXC Technology, we believe strong connections and community are key to our success. Our work model prioritizes in-person collaboration while offering flexibility to support wellbeing, productivity, individual work styles, and life circumstances. We’re committed to fostering an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive.

Recruitment fraud is a scheme in which fictitious job opportunities are offered to job seekers typically through online services, such as false websites, or through unsolicited emails claiming to be from the company. These emails may request recipients to provide personal information or to make payments as part of their illegitimate recruiting process. DXC does not make offers of employment via social media networks and DXC never asks for any money or payments from applicants at any point in the recruitment process, nor ask a job seeker to purchase IT or other equipment on our behalf. We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. We're looking for a Frontend Engineer, Patient Experience & Intakes to help build and improve the patient-facing experiences that power Bask Health's telehealth platform.
